plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value. This is because your payment doesn't depend on your own bid amount (only on the second-highest bid), so bidding higher than value risks negative profit if you win at a price above value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding truthfully at $24 ensures I win only when profitable and maximizes expected profit given the uniform distribution of competitors' values.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($9), I win only when my value exceeds both competitors' bids, and I pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to adjust from, truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value only risks negative profit, and bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform beliefs about opponents' strategies, and since truthful bidding is weakly dominant in this format, I will bid exactly my value of $13.
